Vs.

full_judgment:
Md. Mozammel Hoque, J.: This Rule was issued directing the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the order No. 120 dated 21.8.89 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka, in Miscellaneous Case No. 166 of 1989 affirming the order No. 114 dated 17.5.89 passed in Title Suit No. 47 of 1987 dismissing the suit suo motu as not maintainable for want of consequential relief prayer being not made by the plaintiff-petitioner, should not be set aside. 

 4. Mr. Abu Taher Chowdhury, the learned Advocate, submits that the suit was filed for a declaration that certain Memo issued by the defendant No. 1 is illegal, arbitrary, void and for further declaration that the petitioner is entitled to get the payment of the entire contract. This is purely a suit of declaratory nature. Mr. Abu Taher Chowdhury submits that when the suit was being heard and the evidence of the plaintiff was taken, at that stage suo motu the learned Subordinate Judge passed an order dismissing the suit as not maintainable. He submits that there is no application on behalf of the defendants under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He further submits that in such a matter the case ought to have been disposed of under Order XIV, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Rule 2 of Order XIV of the CPC speaks that where issues both of law and of fact arise in the same suit, and the court is of opinion that the case or any part thereof may be disposed of on the issues of law only, it shall try those issues first, and for that purpose may, if it thinks fit, postpone the settlement of the issues of fact until after the issues of law have been determined. Relying upon the provisions Mr. Abu Taher Chowdhury submits that if the learned Judge deems it fit that the present case can be disposed of only on point of law, then a separate issue is to be framed and after hearing that issue that suit can be disposed of. But in the present case the provisions of Order XIV, rule 2 have been violated in view of the fact that neither any issue was framed on the ground of maintainability nor any date was fixed for hearing and no chance was given to the plaintiff before dismissing the suit in this manner. We find substance in the above contention of Mr. Abu Taher Chowdhury. In a case like this the provisions of Order XIV rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure must be strictly observed. From the prayer of the petitioner it appears to us that this is a suit for mere declaration and in such suit he did not claim any money. Further, if he claims any money, he may be given an opportunity to amend the plaint and pay necessary court-fee. That opportunity was not also given to the plaintiff and as such we find that the learned Subordinate Judge is not at all correct by finding that the suit in the present form is not maintainable. 

 Mr. Sharifuddin Chaklader, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 1, submits that when the order was passed on 17.5.89 dismissing the suit ex parte, the plaintiff ought to have preferred an appeal, but instead of preferring of appeal he filed an application for review under Order XLVII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It is true that no appeal has been preferred against the order dated 17.5.89 but a review application has been preferred. Since, in our view, the order dated 17.5.89 was absolutely illegal and without jurisdiction, we will not entertain such a technical point in a matter like this where the question of substantial justice is involved. Rightly or wrongly, a review application was filed and in that order passed in the review application the earlier order dated 17.5.89 has been affirmed. Now in this Rule the petitioner has challenged the order passed on a review dated 21.8.89 affirming the order dated 17.5.89. If an application under Order XLVII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure is rejected, then the revision will lie. In the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that the ends of justice will be met, if we consider the question of substantial justice in disposing of this Rule. We find that the impugned order dated 21.8.89 affirming the order dated 17.5.89 is illegal and without jurisdiction and the learned Subordinate Judge has committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice in this case. Accordingly, this Rule should be made absolute. 

 5. In the result, this Rule is made absolute and the order dated 21.8.89 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 166 of 1989 affirming the order dated 17.5.89 passed in Title Suit No. 47 of 1987 are hereby set aside and let the Title Suit No. 47 of 1987 be restored to its file and number and it will be proceeded with in accordance with law from the stage where it was stopped.
